Per-run video reports

Every cell of the overnight bitrate & codec ladder, 200 kbps to 8 Mbps, H.264 and AV1. Each report pairs the publisher's send side with the subscriber's receive side over the LiveKit SFU across two 5G links.

1500k-av12000k-h2642000k-av12500k-h2642500k-av13000k-h2643000k-av14000k-h2644000k-av15000k-h2645000k-av16000k-h2646000k-av18000k-h2648000k-av11500k-h264-makeup1000k-h2641000k-av1750k-h264750k-av1500k-h264500k-av1300k-h264300k-av1200k-h264200k-av1
Two latency figures, never one. Transport is capture → arrival (the network, PTP-bound). Local is arrival → pixels (inside the subscriber, including a renderer that has cost 1194 ms on a single frame). Adding them attributes the receiving machine to the link.

Network loss and render skip are separate columns. The funnel on page 1 of each report splits encoded → sent → arrived → decoded → drawn. A single “dropped frames” number spanning both would be a lie.

QP is not comparable across codecs. H.264 runs 0–51, AV1 0–255. Read it down one codec's own column.

PSNR is a measured axis, not a pass criterion. Where the usability threshold sits is the operator's call, not ours.
